glosses: An enclosed space; a courtyard; an uncovered area shut in by the walls of a building, or by different buildings; also, a space opening from a street and nearly surrounded by houses; a blind alley.

examples.text: The girls were playing in the court.
All round the cool green courts there ran a row / Of cloisters, branched like mighty woods, / Echoing all night to that sonorous flow / Of spouted fountain floods.
Goldsmith took a garret in a miserable court.

examples.text: The noblemen visited the queen in her court.

glosses: Attention directed to a person in power; behaviour designed to gain favor; politeness of manner; civility towards someone.

examples.text: No solace could her paramour entreat / Her once to show, ne court, nor dalliance.

glosses: The administration of law.
The hall, chamber, or place, where justice is administered.

examples.text: Many famous criminals have been put on trial in this court.

glosses: The administration of law.

The persons officially assembled under authority of law, at the appropriate time and place, for the administration of justice; an official assembly, legally met together for the transaction of judicial business; a judge or judges sitting for the hearing or trial of cases.

examples.text: The court started proceedings at 11 o'clock.

Next month, Clemons will be brought before a court presided over by a "special master", who will review the case one last time. The hearing will be unprecedented in its remit, but at its core will be a simple issue: should Reggie Clemons live or die?

536(2.1). ... You have the option to elect to be tried by a provincial court judge without a jury; or you may elect to be tried by a judge without a jury; or you may elect to be tried by a court composed of a judge and jury.

glosses: The administration of law.
An organization for the administration of law, consisting of a body of judges with a certain jurisdiction along with its administrative apparatus.

examples.text: Each province in Canada has three courts: a provincial court, a superior court, and a court of appeals.

glosses: The administration of law.
The judge or judges or other judicial officer presiding in a particular matter, particularly as distinguished from the counsel or jury, or both.

examples.text: A case conference in person was convened.... To emphasize that it was a Court proceeding the Court was gowned.

glosses: The administration of law.

glosses: A space prepared and decorated by certain bird species in which to advertise themselves for a mate.

examples.text: The male Wilson's bird of paradise clears an area of rainforest to create a court in which to perform an elaborate mating dance.

glosses: To seek to achieve or win (a prize).

examples.text: He was courting big new accounts that previous salesmen had not attempted.

On the contrary, they employed the brief respite that was left them in fortifying one another's courage, and in bearing testimony to the truth in so earnest a manner that they might almost seem to have courted the crown of martyrdom.

glosses: To risk (a consequence, usually negative).

examples.text: She courted controversy with her frank speeches.

It is not unknown for hot axleboxes to fail completely and for wagons to become derailed as a result. Surely it is courting disaster to allow a train to proceed for up to seven miles with a defective vehicle before it can be brought to a halt?

glosses: To try to win a commitment to marry from.

examples.text: If either of you both love Katharina […] / Leave shall you have to court her at your pleasure.

glosses: To engage in behavior conducive to mating with.

examples.text: The bird was courting a potential mate by performing an elaborate dance.
By one person, however, Portland was still assiduously courted, and that person was the king.

glosses: To attempt to attract; to invite by attractions; to allure.

examples.text: […] a well-worn pathway courted us / To one green wicket in a privet hedge […]
It is a grim, grey old town, standing on bleak, precipitous cliffs that court every passing hurricane, […]

glosses: To attempt to gain alliance with.
To engage in activities intended to win affections.

examples.text: She's had a few beaus come courting.

glosses: To engage in courtship behavior.

examples.text: At this time of year, you can see many animals courting.

glosses: To endeavor to gain someone's affection/support.

examples.text: They're trying to woo the customers back with this new mobile plan.

Behind this carefully crafted strategy of wooing Trump is a desire from Gulf states to solidify and formalize their positions as the US’ indispensable security and economic partners, and extract as much benefit for themselves as they can.

glosses: To try to persuade (someone) to be in an amorous relationship with

examples.text:
Soo leue we syr Launcelot lyenge within that caue in grete payne / and euery day ther came a lady & brouȝt hym his mete & his drynke / & wowed hym to haue layne by hym / and euer the noble knyghte syre Launcelot sayd her nay.
"So leave we Sir Launcelot lying within that cave in great pain; and every day there came a lady and brought him his meat and his drink, and wooed him, to have lain by him; and ever the noble knight, Sir Launcelot, said her nay."
I haue beene wooed, as I intreat thee now, / Euen by the ſterne, and direfull God of warre, / VVhoſe ſinowie necke in battel nere did bow, / VVho conquers where he comes in euery iarre; […]
Each, like the Grecian artist, wooes / The image he himself has wrought.

glosses: To court solicitously; to invite with importunity; to solicit in love.

examples.text: Thee Chauntreſs oft the Woods among, / I woo to hear thy eeven Song;

glosses: Expressing joy or excitement; woohoo, yahoo.

glosses: Alternative form of woo woo.

glosses: Prendre la résolution de faire quelque chose, une action, un ouvrage, et commencer à le mettre à exécution.

examples.text: Nous n’entreprendrons pas une discussion sur les édifices qui ont pu précéder l’église que nous voyons aujourd’hui, […].

glosses: S’engager à faire ou à fournir quelque chose à certaines conditions, surtout en parlant d’ouvrages ou de fournitures considérables.

examples.text: Cet architecte a entrepris tel bâtiment pour telle somme.
Il a entrepris la fourniture des vivres. — Il a entrepris de fournir les vivres pour tel prix.
